sam: Arcadia Systems wants perf numbers before they sign. Scope: chat completions (2k context streaming) + high-throughput embeddings ingest. They care about tight tail latency and predictable bursts. Can eng/ops propose a compact runbook + committed vs burst pricing sketch?
ivy: quick clarifying Qs: model family (13B quant vs fp16), exact p95 target, sustained qps and burst magnitude, embeddings dims?
sam: they prefer quantized 13B if we can meet p95 <= 280ms for token streaming. sustained 100 qps, short 3-minute spikes to 400 qps. embeddings: 1500 reqs/min, 1024-d vectors. Also want an A/B run to compare 13B->7B graceful fallback.
rajesh: proposed approach: four stages 1) auth/sanity smoke 2m, 2) warmup + cache-pop 20m, 3) sustained plateau 40m collect metrics, 4) burst cycles + graceful-fallback test. Also include cold-start blast test and cache-eviction scenario.
ivy: runbook draft:
```
stage 0: auth/smoke - 2m @ 1-3 qps (validate tokens, SSE payload shape)
stage 1: warmup - 20m steady @ 60 qps (populate prefix + KV caches)
stage 2: sustain - ramp to 100 qps over 8m, hold 40m (collect p50/p95/p99, token cost)
stage 3: bursts - 5 cycles: 3m @ 400 qps with 5m cooldowns, include variant fallback to 7B when queue depth > threshold
stage 4: cold-start - terminate one pod, issue 15 concurrent streams to measure tail
metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, request latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, queue length, 5xx rate, fallback events
```
rajesh: loadgen tooling: vegeta for high-QPS non-stream pieces; a tiny SSE harness written in node for streaming. example SSE curl: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream`
rajesh: sample vegeta snippet for embeddings: `echo '{"input":"..."}' | vegeta attack -rate=25 -duration=2m -workers=8 | vegeta report -type=json > embeddings_report.json`
infra-bot: provisioning: dedicated/poc-arcadia -> started 2024-11-21T10:24:00Z :gear:
ivy: infra sketch: sustained 100 qps on 13B-quant -> estimated 4 A100-eq GPUs (conservative). recommend commit 3 units + a 1-unit buffer or commit 4 for predictable latency. bursts to 400 qps -> +4 pre-warmed on-demand GPUs.
sam: rough cost ballpark for procurement (high level only).
ivy: back-of-envelope: commit 3 units -> ~$105k/month; commit 4 -> ~$140k/month. burst on-demand burn: ~$130/hr per GPU * 4 => $520/hr during spikes. note: numbers vary by contract and exact perf profile.
rajesh: failure modes and mitigations to include in the handoff doc: cold-start tails (mitigate via pre-warm and keep-alive), KV cache warming/eviction storms (mitigate via staged warmup + TTL tuning), network fan-in causing queuing (mitigate via token-bucket shaping and ingress throttles), and model degradation under memory pressure (mitigate via automated model swap to 7B variant). we'll also instrument per-route circuit-breaker and graceful 503 with explanation.
emma: security checklist note: Arcadia requires customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred), VPC peering, per-request audit logs for 90 days, and SOC2 + penetration test artifacts. For short POC we can use a temporary key and provide log snapshots; legal will need a signed DPA.
lucas: (Arcadia) I'll share security contact + questionnaire by EOD. We want the fallback behavior documented for our SRE team before sign.
ivy: deliverables: 1) CSV with columns: phase,qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_s,gpu_util_pct,queue_depth,errors_pct,fallback_count 2) 1-page exec summary listing whether p95 SLA met and cost implications 3) short failure-mode appendix.
rajesh: timeline: run smoke + warmup tomorrow 08:00 PT; full run and initial CSV in 36h. I'll own loadgen and aggregation, ivy will own infra sizing & cost, emma will own security steps. sam will collate and send to Arcadia.
sam: action items recap: raijesh (loadgen + results), ivy (infra & cost), emma (security checklist & temporary KMS), lucas (security contact + questionnaire). I'll attach final CSV to CRM and include the 1-pager. :rocket:
lucas: sending contacts now, questionnaire to follow in ~2 hours. thanks team.
sam: great. keep updates in-thread. we'll keep the A/B fallback logs for their SRE review. :thumbsup:
